data.updated: 21 September 2026 (evening — NO LEVEL, GEOGRAPHY OR REVISION-DATE CHANGE on any of the five markets. The evening tier-A sweep asserted complete: 17 sources, exit 0, every one logged, NONE written off as unreachable. ONE REVISION-DATE MOVEMENT WORTH RECORDING, NO SUBSTANTIVE CHANGE: FRANCE DIPLOMATIE’S KENYA SECURITY PAGE NOW CARRIES 18 SEPTEMBER 2026 as its update date, the most recently revised of the five advisories we track. The substance is unchanged and remains the widest of the set: France formally advises against the Kenya–Somalia border zone TO A DEPTH OF 100KM INLAND, against the UK’s 60km Wajir line and the county-level framing used by Canada and Germany. Its standing OCTOBER–DECEMBER clause is unchanged and now close to live: El Niño-accentuated short rains, flash flooding, landslides on road axes including in urban areas, and a resurgence of cholera, typhoid and malaria. Kenya eTA via etakenya.go.ke unchanged. ALL OTHER LEVELS UNCHANGED. UK FCDO KENYA unchanged, page last updated 4 September 2026 and marked current at 19 September: against all travel to Mandera County, Tarbaj and Wajir East constituencies except Wajir Town, Wajir within 60km of the Somalia border, and Garissa County except Garissa Town, Lagdera and Balambala north and west of the Saka-to-C81 road; Nairobi and the main safari circuit unaffected. UK UGANDA unchanged, last substantive update 2 September 2026 recording WHO’s 27 August declaration that the Uganda outbreak is over, plus the 28 August national-cleaning-day exemption note; the UK advises against travel to NO part of Uganda and the 2 December 2025 de-restriction of Queen Elizabeth National Park, south-west Kasese and Semuliki stands. UK TANZANIA unchanged: all-but-essential within 20km of the Cabo Delgado border, and heightened health screening for arrivals from Uganda and the DRC. UK RWANDA unchanged on its 4 September revision: DRC-Ebola border measures, the new vape and e-cigarette ban, Reunion Island entry information, and the warning that the Gisenyi–Goma crossing could close at short notice. CANADA unchanged on Kenya, last updated 9 September 2026, exercise a high degree of caution, avoid all travel to Mandera, Wajir, Garissa and Lamu. GERMANY unchanged. CANADA’S EBOLA BORDER MEASURES STILL EXPIRE 28 SEPTEMBER 2026 AT 23:59 EDT — SEVEN DAYS OUT TONIGHT, down from eight last night. No successor notice published as at this evening. P198 stays OPEN. The US CDC order (91 FR 58673–58679) still expires 4:59pm EDT 11 October 2026. RWANDA ENTRY RULE unchanged and still the strictest in the region: the MoH notice of 22 May 2026 denying entry to foreign nationals who travelled to or transited the DRC in the previous 30 days is unrevised, with NO announced end date, thermal imaging at Gisenyi and screening at all borders and airports, and an Emergency Treatment Centre at Rugerero Sector, Rubavu District. NOTE THE TENSION EXPLICITLY, BECAUSE IT IS NOW ON THE RECORD IN A PRIMARY SOURCE: WHO’s DON617 states that WHO “advises against any restriction of travel to, or trade with, affected countries”. Rwanda’s bar, Canada’s bar and the US order all run against that advice. ZANZIBAR: Travel Advisory No. 1 of 20 May 2026 remains operative — universal non-invasive temperature screening at all air and sea points of entry and a Traveller Surveillance Form for arrivals from or transiting affected areas; Tanzania still records zero Ebola cases. HEALTH — PRIMARY SOURCE READ IN FULL TONIGHT. WHO Disease Outbreak News DON617, published 10 September 2026, fetched and read: as of 7 September the DRC had 6,757 confirmed cases and 3,267 deaths, CFR 48.3%, across 61 health zones in six provinces, with 51 zones in five provinces reporting a case in the last 21 days. Ituri is the epicentre at 5,406 cumulative cases; North Kivu carries 1,066 and the outbreak’s highest CFR at 65.4%; Kayna health zone in North Kivu is the most recently affected. 963 confirmed cases and 481 deaths were added between the 28 August and 10 September DONs. WHO’s 14 August reassessment holds risk VERY HIGH in the DRC, HIGH for land-border neighbours, and LOW for the rest of the African region and globally. There is no licensed vaccine or specific treatment for Bundibugyo; SAGE concluded on 19 August that evidence is insufficient for programmatic use of Ervebo, so it is research-protocol only, with 2,007 frontline workers vaccinated as at 6 September. THE HIGHER FIGURES WE CARRIED LAST NIGHT (7,475 cases and 3,605 deaths to 16 September) COME FROM SECONDARY REPORTING OF WHO/ECDC MATERIAL AND WERE NOT RE-FETCHED TONIGHT — they are retained as Reported, while DON617 is the Confirmed floor. UGANDA: outbreak closed, final toll 20 confirmed cases and 2 deaths, WHO certification 26 August 2026 unchanged. BLIND SPOTS DECLARED: Africa CDC’s posted Epidemic Intelligence Weekly is STILL the AUGUST 2026 edition — no September bulletin published or indexed at time of check. Zanzibar’s Ministry of Health was again not read directly. KCAA’s AIC index showed no new circular in window. TANAPA and NCAA tariff pages showed no new notice. UWA’s July 2024–June 2026 conservation tariff has LAPSED and the replacement is unconfirmed: trade sources cite revised tariffs effective 1 January 2027 but this is NOT matched to a UWA notice, so no Ugandan fee figure is carried.)

us.note: Terrorism, crime, kidnapping, unrest, health and 'Other'. Country level unchanged at 2. Re-issued 28 July 2026 (rendered page carries 'Date issued: July 28, 2026', verified 12 Aug 2026) — the 'Other (O)' indicator was added and the Nairobi neighbourhoods of EASTLEIGH and KIBERA are now LEVEL 4 DO NOT TRAVEL (crime, kidnapping), corrected from our earlier Level 3 reading. Also Level 4: Garissa, Wajir, Mandera, Lamu, Tana River (except Tsavo NP), Kilifi north of the C103 and coastal areas north of Malindi; West Pokot and western Turkana; Marsabit and Turkana within 50km of Ethiopia. Nairobi hotel corridors (Westlands, Upper Hill, Gigiri, CBD, Karen), Diani and Watamu are not in any Level 4 area.

uk.note: Against travel to the Kenya–Somalia border and parts of Lamu/north coast; core safari & coast areas unaffected. HEALTH LAYER (separate from the advisory): three G7 governments now carry a dengue notice on Kenya naming the COAST — US Embassy Nairobi health alert 3 Aug 2026 (coast, Wajir, Garissa); Germany 3 Aug 2026; CANADA added Kenya to Travel Health Notice 517 on 8 Sep 2026. Canada’s notice is Level 1 — practise health precautions — and did NOT change any country risk level. Kenya MoH: 1,678 dengue cases and 5 suspected deaths in Garissa and Wajir as at 26 Aug 2026 (1,276 in Dadaab), PHEOC activated; separately Mombasa recorded 3,989 cases Jan–May 2026 (Health CS Aden Duale via The Standard). The UK has NOT added a dengue line to its Kenya health page as at 9 Sep 2026.

us.note: Do not travel — VERIFIED against travel.state.gov 3 Sep 2026. Date issued 4 June 2026; indicators Crime, Health, Terrorism, Unrest. Advisory history states Uganda was raised from Level 3 to Level 4 on 17 May 2026 'due to the Ebola Bundibugyo Virus Disease outbreak in Ituri Province in the DRC'. The page still describes Kampala mass-gathering restrictions, 21-day quarantine for DRC arrivals and the DRC border closure. NOT UPDATED since 4 June — 91 days — despite Uganda MoH declaring the outbreak over on 28 Jul 2026 and WHO certifying the end on 26 Aug 2026. State's own text links to a CDC travel health notice filed under a Level 2 path. Divergence with the UK (Level 1) is now two full levels.

uk.note: CORRECTED 28 Aug 2026 — the UK advises against travel to NO part of Uganda. We carried 'against all-but-essential travel to Queen Elizabeth & Semuliki NP' for nine months after the FCDO lifted it on 2 December 2025. Verified against gov.uk/foreign-travel-advice/uganda and its Regional risks page, 28 Aug 2026: still current at 25 Aug 2026, updated 27 Jul 2026, and the Warnings page carries no advice-against-travel block at all. Every 'advises against all travel' line on the Regional risks page refers to the DRC and South Sudan, NOT Uganda. Western Uganda carries caution language only (ADF, Kasese/Bundibugyo attacks Nov 2025). Bwindi and Mgahinga are open; armed escort on gorilla tracking is described as routine practice, not a warning. NOTE: mandatory National Cleaning Day, final Saturday monthly 07:00-10:00, nationwide movement restriction — tourists exempt (Uganda Police, 24 Aug 2026).

us.note: Reconsider travel — RAISED from Level 2 to 3 on 31 Oct 2025 ('unrest' indicator added). Grounds: unrest, crime, terrorism (highest risk in the Mtwara Region near the Mozambique border), and targeting of gay & lesbian individuals. Verified vs travel.state.gov 4 Aug 2026.

uk.note: No advisory against travel except within 20km of the Mozambique (Cabo Delgado) border.

us.note: As mainland Tanzania (Level 3 since 31 Oct 2025); no Zanzibar-specific carve-out. Verified 4 Aug 2026.
Reconsider travel — regional Ebola risk and DRC border security.

uk.note: CORRECTED 8 Sep 2026 — the FCDO advice-against area is PARTS OF RUSIZI DISTRICT ONLY: the parts within 10km of the DRC border, including the Rwandan islands in Lake Kivu and Kamembe Airport. RUBAVU IS NOT NAMED. We carried 'Rubavu, Rusizi' and were overstating it — Gisenyi/Rubavu on Lake Kivu carries no advice against travel, and Kigali, Musanze/Volcanoes, Nyungwe and Akagera are all outside the advice-against area. Verified by reading gov.uk/foreign-travel-advice/rwanda/entry-requirements directly on 8 Sep 2026; the page's own public-updated-at is 4 Sep 2026 10:15 BST. ENTRY RULE, separate from the advisory: Rwanda denies entry to any foreign national who has travelled to or transited through the DRC in the 30 days before travel, and runs enhanced screening at Kigali International Airport and DRC land crossings (Rwanda MoH notice, 22 May 2026; FCDO links to RBC for it). Commonwealth citizens get a free 30-day visa on arrival.
